classification.difficultyReason: Sketch two standard trigonometric curves, identify the upper curve over the specified interval and evaluate an exact definite integral.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch the region bounded by the graphs of $y=\sin x$ and $y=\cos x$, and by the vertical lines $x=-\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$.

answer.short: See sketch. The required region lies between the two curves for $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\frac{\pi}{6}$, with $\cos x$ above $\sin x$.
answer.worked: Sketch $y=\sin x$ through $(0,0)$ and $y=\cos x$ through $(0,1)$. Draw the vertical boundaries $x=-\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$. Between these boundaries, $\cos x\ge\sin x$; the required region lies between the curves.

spec.description: Unshaded sine and cosine curves on common arrowed axes, extending beyond dashed vertical boundaries. Curve-name labels are absent, as in the source. Ordinary axes, guides and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: y=sin(x) and y=cos(x); boundaries x=-pi/2 and x=pi/6. Cosine is above sine throughout the bounded interval.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer only; no graph appears in the student prompt.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the area of the region in part a.

answer.worked:
On $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{6}\right]$, $\cos x\ge\sin x$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/6}(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx\\&=\left[\sin x+\cos x\right]_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/6}\\&=\left(\frac12+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)-(-1+0)\\&=\frac{3+\sqrt3}{2}\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$
